I'll start this off by saying this is a mix of a negative review and a timid "Let it cook a bit and see." It's a survivors game, I like playing these and have lots of experience. My review will assume you do too with a TL;DR at the bottom for those who don't have experience or lots of time on these. There is a lot of good, but also just a lot of questions. One big one is Synergies/Evolutions. There aren't any. At all. There are "upgrade benches" that spawn in maps to give you a random trait (They are identical between all guns) on your gun per run. There's really nothing interesting about the guns or gunplay (Quick aside, why is the Uzi burst fire????). Then we can talk about the "spells." Some are cool. I particularly like lightning, tombstone, and the hunger spirit. Ticks, Pentagram, and honestly even the scythe just aren't good. Their activation time is slow, they are close range, or deal such low damage just spend your level up on something else. The game would like you to juggle multiple weapons, it kind of incentives you to with a passive upgrade that reloads other guns while they're not equipped. However, you are significantly better off sticking to a single weapon and stacking all your levels into it than spreading it across weapons. Overall it feels very half baked? There's the systems there but in the literal most basic form. Asking $13 for this in personal opinion is insane. There's more than a usual survivors amount of effort put into the game here given its fps, there's more happening so I understand it not being the insane other direction of Survivors games often costing <$2 USD. In the end I just don't think there's enough here in general, let alone anything very well done to say I'd pay more than like $7-9 USD. TL;DR: It's okayish, if you're looking to jump into survivors games and have fun this isn't it.

Everything about the gameplay hits just right, from the sound and feel of the weapons to the explosions of pixelated gore. It’s just so unfortunate that build diversity and leveling up is so absolutely awful. This game is full of those boring perks other roguelikes have gotten away from like +% damage, health, or pick up radius. None of the upgrades lend themselves to unique builds, create any interesting synergies, or offer any replayability. The other options for upgrades allow you to level up a gun or melee you’re using, but since there is no ammo and no distinction between weapons other than the way they attack, there is little reason to level up multiple weapons. It’s only ever efficient to pick a weapon and choose those upgrades each time they’re offered. There aren’t any choices with weapon upgrades either, as each level of upgrade offers a static bonus. Edit: Nothing about this review has changed in ten hours of playing it. The shooting mechanics are fantastic. Meta progression is weak. Upgrades are uninspired and don't lend themselves to create interesting builds. There is no reason to upgrade multiple weapons. Melee is always worse than ranged because they basically function the same but ranged has no ammo or drop off. I would love for this game to improve. This game fails as a roguelike, and because there is no reason to switch weapons or do anything but move around shooting and surviving, it also fails as a boomer shooter.

The whole game reeks of undisclosed AI-assisted assets, and if it was a linear shooter it wouldn't have an hour and a half of gameplay. And none of that matters since it's part of the mind virus second-monitor dopamine genre of Survivors clones. Gunplay is satisfying, and it's worth the asking price for something to turn your brain off to. To the Devs - please remove the cringeworthy AI achievement descriptions. I don't think a game has made me groan harder than when I killed a golden spider and saw: "Track down and defeat the elusive golden spider. With a swift shot, you’ve claimed your prize—the shimmering golden skull coin. The hunt is on, and your prowess shines brighter than gold!" You really don't need any of that, I understand if English isn't your first language but it makes your game seem extremely cheap.
Notch(the Minecraft guy) suggested it on twitter. Good stuff.

Good, I guess. Pros: -Looks good, feels good -Lots of maps -well crafted. interesting set pieces -custom game mode is a'ight Cons: -Bizarre design decisions across the board -Hold 3-4 weapons but you'd never want more than two, and usually you're best off with just one. -Synergies don't really exist, so just pick the objectively best skill each upgrade. -No real builds, again just pick the objectively best skill -Many characters, but there is little difference in their abilities and game play, just pick the objectively best one (see a theme here?) -more than half the of the interesting skills are locked into late game well after you've beat the game and lost interest (bizarre) -They mislead the player to thinking there is a 3rd act, but it's just a custom game mode -The meta progression is pretty 'meh' and the costs of upgrades vary wildly, if you're a thinky-boy you will identify the best meta upgrades and obtain them quickly and leave the garbage overpriced stuff -CONSUMABLE 'holds' & 'locks', meaning you have to buy new one EACH RUN. One of them costs TEN TIMES as much as the other. again ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bizarre. Want to play with strategy? it will cost you an entire run worth gems to do so, so naturally just don't play strategically because the dev is incentivising you not to. -needs more types of enemies -healing is RNG, sometimes you simply won't have a way to heal and will VERY likely just die through attrition damage late into the game, incredibly frustrating -readability could be improved late into matches when lots of doods are on screen -the voice acting, immediately turned that ♥♥♥♥ off Typical game play loop: 1)Pick the objectively best starter weapon, I mean character. 2)RNG upgrades, hope for starter weapon upgrades, then hope for the objectively best skills, then pray to your chosen deity for the passive health regen skill before things get too hairy. Last resort, pick the healing spell if you cant get the regen, cry 3)run around the map looking for your weapon upgrade workbench, it doesn't cost anything to upgrade but needs to be a certain level. why cant it just upgrade automatically on level since it is free anyways? who knows. Anyways, find that workbench and again pray to your chosen deity for a life steal related upgrade (did you remember to pick the objectively best character at the start? cuz if you didn't your weapon cant roll life steal) 4)OK you're ~8minutes in, you've either hit life gen/steal and 4+levels on your starter weapon; Good job, you need to finish the remaining 22 minutes by face tanking every mob in the game until you win. Otherwise, bad job idiot, you can now begin a slow painful death as you desperately plead with god for any kind of healing. I'm gonna be honest, I don't really want to give a positive review. I am going to though as there is a lot of potential in this game, the bones are there. The game looks and feels great. But it really isn't going to tickle that 'survivors' style game play that you're probably looking for. It's a cheap, shallow imitation right now simply because of poor balance and poor design decisions. I hope a patch comes along a cleans this all up. $5 sale on launch, if it were any higher I would not recommend

不是一般的坐牢，地图也就一两个DUST2那么大，但是一关需要生存二十到三十分钟。别的俯视角游戏还行，这第一人称简直不能更累，而且其他幸存者游戏是越到后面越轻松，这游戏倒是反过来越玩越受苦。 首先就是爆头判定点有大问题，很多怪打头是直接穿模，脖子到下巴的位置才算爆头。然后一大堆花里胡哨的武器结果就双管和近战最有用，谁家的转轮机枪打20发就过热啊连AK都不如。 过了开头几分钟就开始猛猛刷远程和自爆怪，弹幕速度不低，反应时间也就半秒左右，而且一些弹幕是扁平的，不一直左右跑就很容易忽略，自爆伤害只要蹭到边缘就吃满全额，一炸相当于挨二三十发弹幕，再加上地图很小，过个拐角都得小心，还要一直保持专注不然后面一不小心连锁爆炸直接大残，还得生存30分钟真的花钱买罪受。 不过最逆天的还是重投保留剔除这些是消耗品得花钱买，打30分钟就只能买2个重投。
垃圾优化，动不动掉到30帧，玩你吗。 生存30分钟越玩越累，感觉不到升级有啥用，怪的成长远大于自己，还没花里胡哨的技能，一把b枪能打死谁

Game is incredibly shallow, repetitive, easy and boring. You can pass most missions by just running around the map for 20/30 minutes and avoiding exploding enemies (which are the only things that can kill you, but only if you are not paying attention). Weapons feel underwhelming, the things that could potentially be fun are getting held back by design (shotgun swapping gets screwed by reloads, grappling is only allowed in a straight line), the upgrades are incredibly basic (just a % dmg/cd/whatever increase) and there are no synergies.

This game is a lot of fun but I am giving it a negative review because it is supposedly steam deck verified but it runs like straight trash on steam deck. I'm talking below 30 fps frequently. No amount of tweaks with the graphics settings made this run well on my deck. The old school aesthetic is great but it would be nice if the game ran well too. Valve needs to get serious with the steam deck verification system, as it is now it is wholly unhelpful in determining if a game runs well on the deck. I do recommend this game if you have a computer faster than a steam deck.

Bloodshed had the potential to be a fun, old school first person horde survival game, but sadly falls short due to critical flaws in its core mechanics. While the game's 3D old style shooter aesthetic is executed well and sets the perfect stage for a frantic experience, the central gameplay elements fail to deliver, the core mechanics specifically the bland, non synergistic item system result in a repetitive and ultimately boring horde survival experience. The game needs a significant overhaul of its item and power design to deliver on its potential.

Do NOT buy this game if you're looking for a skill-based shooter. This is essentially a first-person idle game, (even with the manual shooting option on), with Chinese-slot-machine-tier "chance" on random upgrades and drops. You WILL be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over, repeatedly, and I'm sure that's the intent. You can check my library for credentials, if you need to -- I don't like anything BUT skill-based games... This ain't it. This right here is what you get if you take a boomer shooter, remove player effort from the equation, and replace it with rapid rolls of the dice... YUCKY! Update: Having played a considerable amount more, now, I've found out what I was missing: You're supposed to suck. You're meant to lose, over and over and over and over and over until that monotony transitions to the tedium of killing enemies without effort for half-an-hour at a time. There's a secret to getting the game as close to fair as possible, though -- Kill 1,000 enemies to unlock Traits for weapons. Whichever character you're playing, immediately find a workbench upon starting a stage. There's a trait that grants you 5% of the damage you deal as self-healing. If it's not at the bench, restart the stage, until it appears. Grab that trait, and focus on upgrading the weapon with that trait. Nothing else you do will matter -- With even 5% healing, you won't lose unless you're TRYING to... Have "fun".
I was having fun until the game referred to an AK47 as 'a symbol of power & resilience'. As soon as I had finished vomiting & decided to apply for a refund.

It's like Doom 2 became a roguelike. It's super gated, could be fun for a few hours but that's it. The unlocks are annoying, the weapons are basic and unimaginative as are the spells. The stages are empty with nothing interesting there, no traps no hidden walls and since it's a rogue lite no coherence. So basically there's not enough there, this game needs 1-2 years of content to be worth paying anything for.

I cautiously recommend this if you can get it on sale. It's not worth its full price. First of all, it's nothing like a boomer shooter apart from the aesthetics. It's firmly a roguelike and ONLY a roguelike. It has too few levels to be long term engaging and too little mechanical depth. Its main purpose is to keep your fingers busy while listening to a podcast or video essay. Gameplay is absolutely braindead. Further, the amount of screen clutter you get in the 30 min survival missions is insane. It's downright impossible to tell what's going on or to identify priority targets among all the stuff all over your screen. The main story missions can be slightly customized after beating the game, but there aren't a lot of them, and most maps aren't fun enough to be played over and over. The trial missions you can unlock by hunting down those golden spiders aren't engaging either. All that being said, the basics are there. The gameplay knows to satisfy with tons of pixel gore underscored by a pretty solid soundtrack, although you'll be turning it off along with the extremely cringe inducing voice lines uttered by the characters which have terminally Millennial writing and delivery. That's why I'm saying it's a podcast game. Best of all, it's only half a gigabyte on your drive and doesn't require a persistent internet connection.

[h1]Bloodshed – Noise Without Depth[/h1] Bloodshed looks intense and plays well enough, but that’s about where the praise ends. The gunplay functions, the enemies explode, and the screen fills with chaos. None of it adds up to anything memorable. Combat is serviceable but [u]shallow.[/u] After a few runs, you’ve effectively seen everything the game has to offer. Enemy variety is minimal, builds blur together, and progression relies too heavily on RNG to feel earned. When the game gets hard, it doesn’t feel demanding—it feels [u]arbitrary[/u]. The presentation is barebones and forgettable. Menus are plain, feedback is weak, and there’s no real sense of identity beyond “retro shooter with lots of enemies.” What should feel brutal and stylish instead comes off as noisy and repetitive. [h3]Verdict:[/h3] Bloodshed kills time, not boredom. It works as a short distraction, but there’s little reason to keep playing once the novelty wears off. Functional, loud, and ultimately [u]hollow[/u].

[h3]Pros:[/h3] [list] [*][b]It's super hectic action[/b], especially at the beginning, when the lack of unlocks pushes for skilful play over tactical upgrade choices. [*]The meta-progression unlocks mostly require reaching level 10 with certain weapons or spells during a run. This incentivises getting to know how each works and planning builds around them, which [b]is quite fun[/b]. [*]Once unlocked, the higher difficulties are actually challenging, [b]punishing mistakes in both skill and tactics[/b]. Skills in the sense of moment-to-moment decision-making, to avoid or prioritise elite units, evade attacks, and nail headshots. And tactics, as in creating a synergetic build and upgrading it on a smooth curve so that it doesn't lack in damage or defence as the enemy waves progress. [/list] [h3]Cons:[/h3] [list] [*][b]The campaign is too short and easy[/b]. I was expecting a third episode and the option to try Hard and Nightmare difficulties from the start. Those only appear on the custom mode that unlocks after beating the whole campaign on Normal. [*][b]There's not that much content[/b]: 8 meta stats upgrades, 15 passives, 15 spells, 7 melee weapons, 11 ranged, and 7 characters. The campaign has 2 episodes of 7 levels each, being 3 regular run maps, a boss fight, a shooting gallery, a speedrun course, and a repeated map with a boss at the end. And so, the custom mode has only 6 maps to mess around with. [*][b]The soundtrack is also lacking[/b], it's a bit generic-sounding and with too few tracks overall. [/list] Grab it on a sale, for sure.

Bloodshed has a lot going for it, but it's not great. It perfectly captures the 90s shooter aesthetic of a proper Doom clone and has pretty good B-movie characters and voice acting, but it doesn't have much variety or depth. There aren't really "builds" because there are so few things to put points into, and like six of the weapons objectively suck. The characters are about as different from eachother gameplay-wise as the different classes in Dark Souls. The enemies are mostly bullet sponges and the hitbox for every character's head is permanently glitched for some reason, so you can't really have any fun perfecting your skills with such a severe built-in aim penalty. Everything takes twice as long as it should. Not only the combat, but the meta-progression between runs and the unlocking of characters and... literally everything. Why are there so few minibosses until the last 10 minutes of a round? Why do so few of the minibosses drop chests? Why do I need to add 8% damage to my shotgun manually instead of incorporating that bonus into a level-up that mattered even 10 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ percent? Does the jump height upgrade have to be perfectly useless even for the guy who can double-jump? Every bonus is nerfed to death, every upgrade is too little too late, and none of the weapons are even adequately powerful. Melee is nonsensically weak. Bloodshed gets a 6.5 out of 10 because it takes what could be a perfect game and smacks you in the face with obviously, painstakingly deliberate design flaws over and over again until you just don't want to try anymore.

This game is extremely unfinished at best. If the game as it is is the complete vision, then it's a failed experience. I like the idea in theory, merging the aesthetic and certain gameplay aspects of Doom with a Vampire Survivors type game, but the levels are too long and monotonous. You fight mostly the same enemies that post no challenge. The upgrades and spells are useless and not fun to use. I think there is a way to make this game fun, but this game isn't in early access, it's a full release, so I'd recommend not buying it or wasting your time on it.

I had fun playing this game. That's it. That's the review. Did I have fun? [ ✓ ] Yes [ ] No That's all the requirements needed for why I choose to spend money on something. [b]IS IT FUN?[/b] Now, keep in mind, ladies and gentlemen of the jury, that I only paid a whopping, staggering, grand total of THREE, yes THREE (3), whole dollars just so I could have fun. And as of being here right here and right now, I have spent a grand total of thirteen, yes THIRTEEN (13), hours enjoying, or as the kids of yonder era are saying, "having fun", said game. So, with that being said, what can I do with THREE US American Dollars in order to, as I quote, "have fun"? - Can I go to the movies for three US American dollars? No. - Can I go buy a baseball bat, baseball and baseball glove for three US American dollars? No. - Can I buy a skateboard for three US American dollars? No. - Can I buy a fishing pole for three US American dollars? No. - Can I go to a bar and hangout for THIRTEEN (13) hours using only three US American dollars? No. - Can I even buy a pair of swimming shorts to go swimming for only three US American dollars? Believe it or not, no. - Can I buy a telescope for three US American dollars? No. - Can I buy hiking boots, a hiking stick, a hiking backpack and trail-mix for three US American dollars? Well, I may be able to carve my own hiking stick, but I'd have to buy a knife. Or I could manually sharpen a rock by striking it against another rock, and then carve the tree branch into a hiking stick. And then I could somehow wrestle a deer, kill the deer with the sharpened rock, skin the deer and MAYBE make boots and a backpack out of the deer, and just eat whatever bugs, berries and mushrooms are around. But that would probably take longer than THIRTEEN (13) hours. And it probably wouldn't be fun. - Can I go to the beach just using three US American dollars? Once again, believe it or not, no. You see, I don't live near the beach. I would have to drive to the beach, and the amount of gas that it would take to drive to the beach would actually, believe it or not, be more than three American US dollars, because I would also have to drive back home. So... no. The point is this: for three American US dollars, I have had THIRTEEN (13) hours of entertainment that nothing else in this world could possibly provide for said amount of currency. So what gives me the right to complain about this source of entertainment that clearly entertained me for less than the cost of a two (2) liter bottle of soda? The Defense rests.

这款第一人称Roguelite射击游戏，核心体验可以用一个字概括：爽。 角色输出速度快，移动速度快，子弹倾泻出去的感觉是顺畅的，击杀反馈也是利落的。尤其是在前期，随便拿把武器冲进敌群，那种“我比怪还能窜”的节奏感确实上头。这种高速战斗带来的肾上腺素分泌，是它最抓人的地方。 角色方面，每个人都有自己的偏好。我比较钟意那个樱花女武士——近战刀砍配合高速突进，前期清图效率极高，手感流畅，一度让我觉得这角色能杀穿一切。只要稍微认真玩，游戏整体难度并不高，任何角色都能顺畅推进。 但爽感的背后，藏着几个绕不开的设计缺陷。 最致命的问题是：高级枪支的获取门槛，高到近乎不存在。 玩了几十把，迷你枪、火箭筒这类本该是后期爽感核心的重火力武器，几乎没见到过。不是运气不好，是系统压根不给。唯一能稳定获取的方式，是用一次性消耗的钻石去抽，而钻石的获取速度又相当有限。换句话说，如果你想体验后期重火力压制的快感，要么氪，要么肝——但肝也不一定肝得到。 这就导致一个尴尬的局面：你永远在用那些前期武器刮痧，爽感被硬生生卡在一个不上不下的位置。 另一个问题是角色设计的后期失衡。樱花妹前期确实爽，刀刀烈火，砍瓜切菜。但到了后期，问题就暴露了——游戏几乎不给你远程枪支，被动技能倒是塞了一大堆。一个近战角色在远程火力主导的后期关卡里，生存压力陡增。冲进去容易，出不来也容易。这种前后期的割裂感，让人怀疑角色设计是不是根本没做完。 至于内容量，这款游戏属于典型的“爽一下可以，久玩不行”。任务系统还算丰富，偶尔拿起来突突两把，解压效果不错。但如果你试图把它当主游，每天刷，很快就会触到重复感的底。关卡变化有限，Build套路也单一，加上高级武器获取难，后期基本就是在重复前期的流程——只是数值更高了，体验却没变。 总结来说：这是一款手感在线、爽感前置、后期乏力的轻度Roguelite射击游戏。适合碎片时间发泄，不适合深度投入。如果你只是想找一款“拿起来就能爽一把”的替代品，它合格；但如果你想找一款能长期深耕的Build型射击Roguelite，它的底子还不够厚。 爽是真的爽，腻也是真的腻。 评分体系 艺术性4 游戏性5 创意性4 深度性5 社交性1 操作性8 剧情性4 总体评分5.5 短评：适合路一发

[h1]A Bloody Mess[/h1] [b]Bloodshed = Blood + Shed + 1999 Cringe + Hexen + Army of Darkness + Broken Roguelite[/b] It's pretty clear what the game is at least trying to do here, and honestly, it half succeeds! It has all the right unc vibes. The graphics, from the enemy sprites, the characters, and environments, are straight uncle-bait. If you played games like Blood or Hexen, your eyes will immediately be drawn to this game and it's attempts to looksmaxx you. To it's credit, I did think that many of the designs were pretty great, even occasionally terrifying. The audio in terms of sound effects are punchy and chunky, and the game does a fair job at keeping you situationally aware based on audio cues (the anxiety definitely starts to kick in when you hear the banshee wails coming closer). The auto-shooting is mostly competent, the environments are good enough with some actually being really neat conceptually, and there's a good-enough boss battle at the end. The playable characters are, to the very last of them, 300% cringeworthy. However, to be fair, this really does keep with the theme of the era the games and movies that were the muses for this one. But there are only TWO acts, and the game leans heavily on very expensive upgrade costs for replay value. Still, it's not wrong for games to be short, I think the idea that every game needs to be a 200 hours epic is silly, and that some games are just fine as short little "snacks". That said, and as many reviewers have pointed out, the balance is so very terrible in this game that it is actually confusing. So many other elements are competent or even good, I didn't run into any bugs, the audio and visuals are great... Did no one care about balance? I am not kidding when I tell you that 9/10 weapons in this game are straight up not worth using, and some of them are just way too similar to one another. This also holds true for the character selection. All of them are just BAD when compared to Seraphina. Why? Because her starter weapon is THE BEST WEAPON IN THE GAME and her secondary isn't occupied with a worthless melee weapon but rather one of the somewhat useful spells. This means no hoping to roll a better weapon, and no levels or slot-machine rolls wasted on upgrading a weapon you will never use. With the minor exception of the sawed-off shotgun, EVERY other starter weapon is worthless even when upgraded, or needs a specific set of upgrades to make them not feel terrible by the time you get midway through the run. The staff? As soon as you hit 3 projectiles with that thing, you will be mowing down enemies, including bosses, like child's play. Even without upgrades that make it even more comically OP. [i]Shed some blood if you...[/i] [list] [*]Want a decent "snack" of a game that's good to veg out to while you have a video playing. [*]Need a dose of late 90s/early 2000s nostalgia and don't want to commit to a more serious game but also don't feel like replaying Heretic or Blood for the thousandth time. [*]Just need to keep that survivors-like dopamine flowing and you come across this game on sale and are fiendin' [/list] [i]Go watch Buffy the Vampire Slayer instead if you...[/i] [list] [*]Need something you can sink some significant time into [*]Are looking for lots of unlocks and skill trees and meaningful build-making [*]Can't stand an unbalanced game because GOOD GOD [/list] I know I really torched this game in this review, but I am going to be honest. I DID like it. It's kinda like... When you are drunk or really high and you get Jack In The Box tacos at 2am. Are they good tacos? Mmm, no man. No they are not. BUT, for that short moment? They just hit. [u][h2]BOTTOM LINE [/h2][/u] Blood was not shed, but nor were my tears. [h3]Jack in the Box Tacos/10.[/h3]

I might play this a bit more in the future, I don't hate it or anything, but I need to be completely and totally transparent with you if you're planning on getting this. This is a mixture of Vampire Survivors and classic boomer shooters like Doom and Blood, but it EXPONENTIALLY leans in way more to being a VS game, and I think that's massively to the game's detriment. The first red flag is the game has automatic-shooting on by default, like what kind of FPS fan on gods green earth wants the game to shoot FOR you? The entire POINT of this genre is to shoot stuff yourself- and yes, it's a toggleable option, but again, it's a red flag and the game's general balancing screams it. There's no hit-scan enemies to demand you use cover, there's no projectile tracking that I can tell, boss enemies typically just run towards you but are never fast enough to catch up, it's very easy to just build into a single weapon and ONLY use that weapon since there's no ammo to speak of, there's SOOOO many ways to heal and stun enemies that get too close to you to invalidate melee threats, amounting to a VERY easy "shooter" experience. This, mixed with games going anywhere from 15-30 minutes, very quickly overstays its welcome. And the cherry on top? The voice lines in the game are pretty annoying. I get it's boomer shooter inspired, boomer shooter protags quip all the time, but a lot of the lines say something that is funny, but then drag out the joke one sentence longer than it should, ruining the entire voiceline. You can turn that off if you want to but I really wish the writing was just a bit more on point. Again, I don't hate the game, the graphics are VERY good, the pixel gore is great, actually shooting does feel good, I just feel like the devs leaned too much into this being a casual game, and it really does not compliment what I believe the intended audience is. I really hope they take this sort of criticism into account if they make something else like this, because I can tell they are extremely talented, I just think they took a wrong turn here.

I wrote a pretty lengthy review here but decided to erase it as I've figured out that I'm pouring my soul out for a game that doesn't really deserve anymore of my time. Instead all I will say is that I'm disappointed. Beyond disappointed. Infuriated even with how the game ended up being. All that was done here was take a popular concept from a popular game without realizing what made that game popular in first place. Could it be the amazing item synergies / evolutions and character synergies along with it's simple gameplay loop? Nah, clearly what people need is some horde survival roguelite copy'n'paste staring revolutionary upgrade system and your unfinished breakfast from yesterday where you click and wonder where your bullet went, all while having barely readable enemy projectiles assault your prostate without your consent. Did it actually hit the enemy? No lmao, it went through it's sprite as hitboxes here aren't even properly rigged to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemy sprite. You have movement where you can strafe jump and gain insane speed but what else is to do here? Nothing. Two chapters, some repeat bonus missions you unlock for finding unlockables and gg, you're done. Here have some guns and crap where majority of it hits like a limp ♥♥♥♥ to the face but wait! You can throw items to upgrade them! All you need to do is hope that RNG in the game gives you the upgrades you need <3 Yes dear <user>, we have decided to make items be fully RNG driven selections with no permanent banishments so you can always never build what you want. You're welcome. Wow I wonder why this small mysterious indie game called "Vampire Survivors" HAD A WAY TO PERMANENTLY BANISH ITEMS FROM THE POOL? MAYBE IT WAS DONE TO MAKE IT FUN AND LESS RELIANT ON RNG?!?!?! WHO WOULD'VE THOUGHT, WOW! I must've discovered America with this! Why reinvent the wheel when it was perfectly fine before? Coming back to this game after my first playthrough (near 100%) a while back, I'm noticing a common gripe within the reviews is the limited amount of content and short overall playtime. I do fully agree that if the devs gave this game a longer release cycle and filled it with more of the same (new characters, weapons, maps), this game could've been something even more special. But for what it is, a cool mesh of boomer shooter and survivor game, they really nail it, and there's few other games on the market that mesh those genres - none of which do it as well as this game. In my recollection, I never felt any feelings of "that's unfair, they need to rework that". Sure, there's runs where you continuously end up getting terrible upgrade selections, but that's the reality of roguelikes/lites. But overall, the design, graphics, and sway between "oh man I'm underpowered and need to catch up on upgrades" to "I don't know if it's even possible for me to lose this run anymore" that I find to be a hallmark of survivor games is all there and done well. To go back to my original point about the length: If you consider the price tag, the $13 they're charging feels fair, not great. Get it on sale, have a blast for some hours bingeing it, scrap out a few more hours going for completion if you like, and maybe come back to do it all over again sometime later. And btw, it goes on sale frequently for $3-4, not even factoring in the bundle discounts that this game has plenty of.

Bloodshed is an old-style shooter with roguelike elements. As one of several heroes, you are tasked with surviving and fighting hordes of monsters in a fairly short campaign while gathering temporary upgrades and dodging everything you can. In the hub area, you spend your gold on permanent upgrades to facilitate your next run. The game is fairly simple and easy. Throughout its completion, I never felt it was unfair or particularly difficult. The seven heroes are quite distinct and require different approaches to gameplay, but they all benefit equally from the same spells and passive abilities. Bloodshed has only two chapters and can be completed within a couple of hours. It is a nice game to spend a few days with if you are a fan of chaotic shooters.

TLDR: Avoid. Hollow and tediously boring gameplay loop with horrible balanced in-game meta economy that's shallower than the tub water when you shower. Not worth your money or time. If you enjoy boomer shooters and want a small dabble of survivors-like elements, then you'll enjoy this game. If you enjoy survivors-like or actual, proper rogue like (or rogue lite) then you won't like this game. The game is incredibly shallow and you'll find yourself bored within the hour. That said, I came into this expecting a proper survivors-like, bullet heaven, roguelikes, or roguelite game and was left disappointed after the first couple missions and extremely bored. The devs don't even use the right game tags for this. The game description has 'roguelite' and the store tag has 'roguelike' and yes there's a difference even though many of us (myself included) often use them interchangeably. However, in a game like this where you're interested in trying a fusion of various genre elements or mechanics, it matters a tad more in my opinion. In each run (mission) you can collect gems that will persist regardless if you win or lose. You'll then use those for meta upgrades such as increased dmg or armor or to unlock other characters. One unique and cool thing you can do with gems is buy a revive. It's obscenely expensive, but it's an item that carries through multiple missions until you use it. I think it adds some good weight to the gameplay and whether or not you want to invest in the obscene cost of it. The games meta and unlock with gem economy is pure garbage. In the first mission I got about 30 gems in a 5 minute mission, understandable. The next mission was 20 minutes and I got around 400 or so. Okay, so I weighed unlocking another character or doing a meta upgrade for a very specific item that doesn't apply to every character. Hm, okay. Well, the 3rd mission is 30 minutes but at this point I couldn't bother to commit to 30 minutes for one mission because it was so tediously boring and with minimal rewards to boot. I just don't like this game. The only roguelite elements is obscenely expensive upgrades at costs that don't respect your time. There seem to be more meta upgrades you can unlock the more you play along with additional characters and weapons and in-mission only unlocks. But it's all ruined by the utterly boring gameplay. The game defaults to auto-shoot (as is normal in top down survivors likes) so you can focus on movement, kiting, and dodging projectiles. But honestly that just exacerbated the boredom even more because avoiding damage and kiting enemies is incredibly easy. So, I tried manual shooting. More boredom. There's no weight to your punches unless you invest in upgrades. And only invest in one weapon despite having an arsenal of options. I'm very disappointed I didn't like this more and surprised at how many reviews are positive. That was until I noticed how many of the positive reviews have very little playtime overall. It's a very short game. Perhaps that is why the devs made the gameplay loop so tedious and rewards so scarce. It's too bad I spent more time and thought into this review than the devs did in creating a proper gameplay loop that is fun, worth your time, and worth $13. I'm thankful I got it for $4 and I'd refund it if I didn't wait to play it.
